Most enterprise bots sound smart but hallucinate when asked about your real policies and data. This episode is for architects and IT leaders choosing between Copilot Studio and Azure AI Foundry. You learn how RAG works, where each platform shines and a simple framework for when to migrate.

In this episode
  • 00:00 – Why most bots are just fancy parrots: RAG and access control
  • 03:38 – Copilot Studio: quick wins with training wheels
  • 08:07 – Azure AI Foundry: the enterprise AI factory
  • 12:01 – The three-tier framework: explore, scale, govern
  • 16:05 – The hidden gotchas Microsoft glosses over
  • 19:15 – Pick your poison wisely

Key takeaways
  • Retrieval-augmented generation with identity-aware access control is what turns a hallucinating chatbot into an assistant grounded in your tenant data.
  • Copilot Studio delivers fast low-code pilots but hides model controls, while Azure AI Foundry exposes models, evaluation, MLOps and audit trails at the cost of time and skills.

Your Copilot Studio agent looks perfect in the test pane, then fumbles in Teams and starts inventing policy answers. This episode is for makers building their first agents and shows how grounding, a defined persona, a tight debug loop and channel-by-channel testing turn a confident guesser into a bot that cites its sources.

In this episode
  • 00:00 – From natural one to natural twenty
  • 00:38 – Why your perfect test bot collapses in the wild
  • 03:43 – The rookie mistake: leaving your bot ungrounded
  • 07:20 – Teaching your bot its personality
  • 11:40 – Debugging the fumbles in real time
  • 14:58 – Publishing and channel surprises
  • 18:28 – Recap: ground, persona, pilot

Key takeaways
  • Test every topic with clean, casual and typo-ridden variations and broaden trigger phrases, because the Copilot Studio test pane is tidier than real users.
  • Ground the agent in trusted knowledge sources such as an uploaded policy file, wait for indexing and limit critical topics to those sources so conversational boosting cannot fill gaps with guesses.
  • Treat publishing as another test phase: retest in Teams, SharePoint and the demo website
